artiest/ray-charles.text:
Ray Charles Robinson was born in 1930 in Albany, in the state of Georgia, and grew up in Florida. At the age of three he heard boogie-woogie on the piano in a café, and the owner taught him to play. By about the age of seven he was blind. At a school for the deaf and the blind he learned classical piano and how to read music in Braille. After his mother's death he spent his teens travelling between bands in Florida and in 1948 left for Seattle, where he got to know the young Quincy Jones. At first he took Nat King Cole as his model.

In 1952 Atlantic Records bought his contract. At the end of 1954 he recorded I Got a Woman, a song that goes back to a gospel song by The Southern Tones and that brought together gospel, jazz and blues. In 1959 came What'd I Say, a blend of gospel, jazz, blues and Latin American music, his first big pop hit. At ABC he then became one of the first Black musicians to be granted artistic freedom at a major label. Georgia on My Mind (1960) became a number one, and with Modern Sounds in Country and Western Music (1962) he brought country and rhythm and blues together.

Charles sang with a raw, churchy voice and accompanied himself on piano, often with the women's chorus The Raelettes and a big band behind him. By coupling the worldly lyrics of the blues with the form and the rapture of gospel, he gave soul its shape in the 1950s. Colleagues called him The Genius. He died in 2004.
artiest/ray-charles.listen: Listen to I Got a Woman and notice the singing: Charles exults and calls out like a preacher in church. Hear how that gospel rapture here carries a song about a girlfriend.

artiest/ray-davies.text:
Ray Davies is an English singer and songwriter, born in 1944 in Muswell Hill in north London. Together with his brother Dave he founded The Kinks in the early 1960s, the band of which he became the singer and chief writer. The group broke through in 1964 with You Really Got Me, a song with a raw, distorted guitar sound that anticipated much later rock and punk.

Davies then increasingly wrote songs that were not about love in general but about ordinary English life. Waterloo Sunset from 1967 looks at two people and the river in London, and the 1968 album The Village Green Preservation Society sings of village customs and vanishing things. In 1970 came Lola, a hit about an encounter in a club in Soho. His songs often have characters and small stories, sometimes with a smile and sometimes with a sharp edge.

Davies was regarded as one of the first writers to make everyday British life a subject for pop music. In the course he is the example that Blur later followed, when that band wrote songs about characters and situations from contemporary England. Incidentally, the name Ray Davies should not be confused with that of the trumpeter of the same name from the British studio circuit.
artiest/ray-davies.listen: Listen to Waterloo Sunset and notice the soft, swaying melody and the images in the lyrics, in which the singer looks at other people from his window. What kind of story does this song tell?

artiest/ray-manzarek.text:
Ray Manzarek was an American keyboard player, singer and producer. He was born in 1939 in Chicago, to parents of Polish descent. He played piano in a jazz band at university and studied economics, and later film at UCLA in Los Angeles. There he got to know Jim Morrison. Shortly after their studies they bumped into each other by chance on Venice Beach. Morrison sang him a few songs, including Moonlight Drive, and Manzarek wanted to start a band straight away. At a lecture on transcendental meditation he found the guitarist Robby Krieger and the drummer John Densmore. That is how The Doors came into being in 1965.

The band first played in clubs on the Sunset Strip, such as the Whisky a Go Go, and signed with Elektra Records. The Doors had no bass player. On stage Manzarek therefore played the bass lines with his left hand on a Fender Rhodes keyboard bass, while playing organ with his right. His best-known sound was that of the Vox Continental organ, which could be heard on much psychedelic rock of the time. His playing, with influences from jazz and classical music, gave the long, dreamy songs of The Doors their colour. He also sang the second voice behind Morrison.

After Morrison's death in 1971 Manzarek made two more albums with the band. Later he made solo records and a rock version of Carmina Burana, and he produced the first four albums of the punk band X. In 1993 he was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame with The Doors. He died in 2013.
artiest/ray-manzarek.listen: Listen to Riders on the Storm from 1971. Notice the soft, dripping sound of Manzarek's Rhodes piano and the sound of rain and thunder mixed in beneath it.

artiest/ray-slijngaard.text:
Ray Slijngaard is a Dutch rapper and singer, born in 1971, who is best known as one half of the Eurodance duo 2 Unlimited. That project was set up in 1991 by the Belgian producers Jean-Paul De Coster and Phil Wilde. Slijngaard was asked to write a rap for one of their songs. He also came up with a chorus for a female singer and brought in Anita Doth for it. The demo went down well, and so the group around Ray and Anita came into being.

The first single was Get Ready for This, which was picked up in Europe and beyond, including at sporting events. After that came, among others, Maximum Overdrive, No Limit, Tribal Dance, The Real Thing, Twilight Zone and Workaholic. Slijngaard rapped on most of the tracks, in a deep, rhythmic voice over fast dance rhythms and hard synthesizers. He also stood out for his hairstyle, with a shaved head and a few dreadlocks on the forehead.

In 1996, after four albums, the group stopped. Slijngaard started a record company of his own and worked on new projects, and in 2009 he was on stage again together with Anita Doth. His role shows how the face of a dance act can also be a writer and co-originator, while the music itself came into being in the producers' studio.
artiest/ray-slijngaard.listen: Listen to No Limit and notice the interplay between Ray's rap and Anita's sung chorus. How do the hard synthesizers and the tight rhythm make the hook stick?

artiest/raymond-rasch.text:
Raymond Rasch was an American pianist and arranger who worked in Hollywood in the 1950s and 1960s. He was born on 1 March 1917 in Toledo, Ohio, and died on 23 December 1964. Not much more is recorded in the sources, and what is known about him is mainly his work behind the scenes.

His name is linked to one film: Charlie Chaplin's Limelight from 1952. Chaplin wrote the music himself, but could not notate it, and so needed people to work out and orchestrate his melodies. Rasch was one of them. The film contains the theme that later became known as a song. It took a long time for the music to win a prize: only in 1972 was the film shown in Los Angeles, and that made it eligible for an Oscar. Rasch won the Oscar for best original score posthumously that year, together with Chaplin and Larry Russell.

In this way Rasch is an example of the many arrangers and pianists who helped shape the sound of popular music without their names becoming known to the public. He died more than seven years before he received the prize. Anyone who sees and hears the film experiences, at any rate, the result of his craftsmanship, in a score that sounds both sentimental and elegant.
artiest/raymond-rasch.listen: Listen to the main theme of Limelight, which Chaplin wrote and Rasch helped work out. Notice the soft, singing melody and the way the orchestra carries it.

artiest/red-garland.text:
William McKinley Garland, known as Red Garland, was an American jazz pianist, born on 13 May 1923 in Dallas and died on 23 April 1984. He began on clarinet and alto saxophone and learned piano in the army, where he was also an amateur boxer and even faced Sugar Ray Robinson. After his military service he went on teaching himself with exercise books by Czerny and Hanon and took Count Basie as his model. In 1946 he stayed on in New York and played, among others, for Billy Eckstine.

His breakthrough came in 1955, when he joined the quintet of Miles Davis, with John Coltrane, Philly Joe Jones and Paul Chambers. Together they made the Prestige albums Workin', Steamin', Cookin' and Relaxin', and Garland played on 'Round About Midnight from 1957 and on Milestones. His block-chord style can be heard clearly on those records. Miles had asked him to bring something of Ahmad Jamal's lightness into his playing. Some listeners called him a cocktail pianist; Davis himself was satisfied.

Afterwards he led groups of his own and recorded many albums, such as Red Garland's Piano in 1957, Red in Blues-Ville in 1959 and Soul Burnin' in 1964. He helped make block-chord playing popular in jazz piano. His playing sounds relaxed and swinging, with chords that lie like a carpet beneath the soloist.
artiest/red-garland.listen: Listen to Cookin' or Relaxin' by the Miles Davis Quintet and notice what the pianist does while Miles and Coltrane solo. Do you hear how Garland fills the space with loose chords?

artiest/red-hot-chili-peppers.text:
Red Hot Chili Peppers is an American rock band from Los Angeles, founded in 1982. The singer Anthony Kiedis and bass player Flea knew each other from Fairfax High School, and formed the band with guitarist Hillel Slovak and drummer Jack Irons. The group blended funk with punk and rock and so became one of the best-known bands of funk rock.

Their second album, Freaky Styley (1985), was produced by George Clinton of Parliament-Funkadelic. In 1988 Slovak died of a heroin overdose. His place was taken by the young guitarist John Frusciante, and at the end of 1988 Chad Smith joined on drums. In 1991 the band recorded Blood Sugar Sex Magik, with producer Rick Rubin, at The Mansion, a studio in a house in Laurel Canyon. The first single, Give It Away, revolves around a bouncing bass line from Flea, over which Kiedis repeats the title like a chant. The song became the band's first number one on the American Modern Rock chart and won a Grammy in 1993. The ballad Under the Bridge reached number 2 on the Billboard Hot 100. The album has sold more than twelve million copies.

With Californication (1999) the band became bigger still. The group has sold more than 120 million records worldwide and was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2012. The combination the band found early on, Kiedis's rapped vocals over Flea's slap bass, remained the core of the sound. In this way the funk of the 1970s lived on in rock.
artiest/red-hot-chili-peppers.listen: In Give It Away, listen to Flea's bass: he slaps and pulls the strings (slapping), so that every note sounds like a dry crack, and the line leaps across almost the whole neck of the bass. Also hear John Frusciante's guitar solo: it was recorded and then laid backwards over the music.

artiest/redone.text:
RedOne is the stage name of Nadir Khayat, a Moroccan-Swedish producer, songwriter and singer. He was born on 9 April 1972 in Tétouan, Morocco, the ninth and youngest child. In 1991, at the age of nineteen, he moved to Sweden, because so much good music came from there. He named ABBA, Europe and Roxette as major influences. He began as a rock musician, but in 1995 he chose to write and produce songs for others. He took the name RedOne from the nickname of a friend, Redouan.

Important for his change of course was Rami Yacoub, a Swedish producer who taught him how to work with programming and software. Together they wrote songs, including for the Swedish girl group Popsie. After that he produced for Swedish and European pop acts, and in 2001 and 2002 he worked on A*Teens, a group that had started out as an ABBA tribute band. Later he worked with artists such as Lady Gaga, Jennifer Lopez, Enrique Iglesias, Pitbull, One Direction, Nicki Minaj and Usher.

In 2009 he was the leading producer on the Billboard Hot 100. He won three Grammys, received eight nominations and in 2010 founded a label of his own. Since 2021 he has been Creative Entertainment Executive at FIFA. His sound combines dance, pop, house, hip hop and R&B in a smooth, dance-floor-oriented production. He is an example of the producer as the defining force behind other people's hits.
artiest/redone.listen: Listen to a track by Lady Gaga that RedOne worked on, such as Just Dance, and notice the solid electronic beat and the repetition of the melody in the chorus.

artiest/reggy-tielman.text:
Reggy Tielman was guitarist of the Tielman Brothers, the first Dutch-Indonesian band to have success on the international stage in the 1950s. The group was formed by four children of Herman Tielman from Kupang in eastern Indonesia and Flora Lorine Hess: Andy on vocals and guitar, Reggy on guitar, Ponthon on bass and Loulou on drums. They grew up in Indonesia, where they first performed under the names Timor Brothers and The Four T's.

In 1956 the family moved to the Netherlands, first to Breda and later to The Hague. The brothers stood out for their spectacular show, with guitars flying through the air. In 1958 they played at the world exhibition in Brussels in the Dutch pavilion. Hired as filler for fifteen minutes, they seized their chance: they threw instruments to one another and Ponthon played the bass with his teeth. Performances in German clubs followed, including on the Reeperbahn in Hamburg. Their 1958 single Rock Little Baby of Mine is regarded as the first Dutch rock 'n' roll record.

The band played a kind of rock 'n' roll that was later called Indorock, a blend of Indonesian and Western music with roots in kroncong. In Germany they grew into a popular live act; in the Netherlands they remained less well known. In early 1964 Andy and Reggy were injured in a serious car accident in Germany, after which the line-up changed often. In 1990 there was a reunion concert, without Reggy and Ponthon. Reggy died in March 2014, the last of the four brothers, at the age of eighty.
artiest/reggy-tielman.listen: Listen to Rock Little Baby of Mine and notice the guitars. Do you hear how a Dutch group in 1958 took over rock 'n' roll from America and gave it a twist of its own?

artiest/reid-anderson.text:
Reid Anderson is an American bass player and composer, born on 15 October 1970 in Minnesota. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Eau Claire and graduated from the Curtis Institute of Music. He is best known as a member of The Bad Plus, a band with drummer Dave King and pianist Ethan Iverson. The original line-up first played together in 1989 and formally founded the band in 2000. Later Anderson also worked with saxophonist Chris Speed and guitarist Ben Monder.

Besides The Bad Plus he played on the New York jazz scene with his own group. His own albums are Dirty Show Tunes from 1997, Abolish Bad Architecture from 1999 and The Vastness of Space from 2000. With The Bad Plus he recorded the album The Bad Plus in 2001 and These Are the Vistas in 2003 for Columbia Records. Give followed in 2004 and Suspicious Activity? in 2005. He also played on albums by Uri Caine, Fred Hersch and Ethan Iverson.

The Bad Plus showed that a jazz trio could do more than play standards. For Anderson himself, the double bass is the fixed centre of his work: he is both bass player and composer, and plays in both permanent groups and changing line-ups.
artiest/reid-anderson.listen: Listen to a track from These Are the Vistas and notice the double bass. Do you hear how the bass does not just accompany but also plays melodies itself?

artiest/reinbert-de-leeuw.text:
Reinbert de Leeuw was a Dutch conductor, pianist and composer. He was born on 8 September 1938 and died on 14 February 2020. His parents were both psychiatrists. He had piano lessons from the age of seven, studied music theory and piano in Amsterdam and composition with Kees van Baaren at the Royal Conservatoire in The Hague, where he later taught himself. From 2004 he was a professor in Leiden.

In 1974 he founded the Schönberg Ensemble, which focused mainly on the Second Viennese School and the avant-garde. He conducted the major Dutch orchestras, including the Royal Concertgebouw Orchestra, and was a guest in Europe, the United States, Japan and Australia. At De Nederlandse Opera he directed productions of, among others, Stravinsky, Louis Andriessen, Ligeti and Britten. In 2011 he conducted Schönberg's Gurre-Lieder, a long-cherished wish. He was also the founder of the Dutch Charles Ives Society.

As a pianist he recorded, among other things, Vexations, the famous, extremely repetitive piece by Erik Satie, and The Early Piano Works of Satie. He also played Pierrot lunaire and Messiaen's Quatuor pour la fin du temps. His albums show how broad his interests were, from Satie and Ives to the Viennese school. He made new music and forgotten music accessible to a large audience, and so left his mark on Dutch musical life.
artiest/reinbert-de-leeuw.listen: Listen to his recording of Vexations by Satie and notice how one short sequence of chords keeps returning. Does the music change, or mainly your way of listening?

artiest/reinier-baas.text: The guitarist Reinier Baas studied at the Amsterdam conservatoire. His albums were given titles such as More Socially Relevant Jazz Music (2011) and Smooth Jazz Apocalypse (2014). Baas often collaborates with young Dutch and foreign musicians, such as the saxophonist Ben van Gelder, and plays both acoustic jazz and experimental music. His pieces often have funny titles and surprising twists. He belongs to a generation that learned jazz at the conservatoire and that blends it with pop, rock and contemporary composed music. He is one of the best-known guitarists of the new Dutch jazz.
artiest/reinier-baas.listen: Notice the surprising twists in composition and guitar playing.

artiest/rene-clemencic.text:
René Clemencic was an Austrian composer, conductor, harpsichordist, clavichordist and recorder player. He was born on 27 February 1928 in Vienna and died on 8 March 2022, at the age of ninety-four. He studied at the University of Vienna and then in France, the Netherlands and West Germany. He led the Capella Musica Antiqua and the Drama Musicum in Vienna.

In 1958 he founded Musica Antiqua, from 1959 the Ensemble Musica Antiqua, to perform early music on period instruments. In 1968 came the Clemencic Consort. With that ensemble he recorded a great deal of medieval and Renaissance music, such as Troubadores in 1986, Carmina Burana in 1990 and Danses de la Renaissance in 1992. His 1976 album René Clemencic et ses flûtes presents him as a recorder player.

As a composer he wrote, among other things, Missa Mundi from 1981, the ballet Drachenkampf from 1987, the oratorio Kabbala from 1992, the oratorio Apokalypsis from 1996 and the chamber plays for the sirene Operntheater, such as Nachts unter der steinernen Brücke in 2009 and the oratorio Gilgamesch in 2015. He also wrote the film music for Ariane Mnouchkine's Molière from 1978. In this way he linked old sounds with new compositions. He is among the pioneers of the movement that brought early music back to life for a large audience.
artiest/rene-clemencic.listen: Listen to his recording of Carmina Burana, which takes the medieval songs as its starting point. Notice the sound of the instruments, which is different from that of a symphony orchestra.

artiest/rene-urtreger.text:
René Urtreger was a French bebop pianist, born on 6 July 1934 in Paris to Polish Jewish immigrants. He began piano lessons at the age of four, studied at the conservatoire and played in a small Paris club, where Sacha Distel and Jean-Louis Viale also performed. In 1953 he won a piano competition for amateurs and decided to become a professional musician.

In 1954 he accompanied the American saxophonist Don Byas and trumpeter Buck Clayton in Paris. After his military service he played at the Club Saint-Germain, on the Left Bank of the Seine, where he worked with Miles Davis and Lester Young. Young was so impressed that in 1956 Urtreger went on a short tour of Europe with him. In December 1957 he played in the group of Miles Davis that recorded the music for the film Ascenseur pour l'échafaud. In the late 1950s he played with, among others, Lionel Hampton, Stan Getz, Chet Baker, Dexter Gordon, Sonny Rollins and Ben Webster. In 1961 he received the Prix Django Reinhardt.

His first album, Jazz in Paris: René Urtreger joue Bud Powell, appeared in 1955. Later he also wrote film music, including for Claude Berri. In 1977 he returned to the Paris jazz scene and played with, among others, Lee Konitz and Barney Wilen. His playing is known as sensitive, with a full, dense swing. He himself said that jazz should be music of improvisation and madness. Urtreger died on 16 July 2026.
artiest/rene-urtreger.listen: Listen to his album Jazz in Paris: René Urtreger joue Bud Powell and notice how a Parisian pianist makes the bebop of Bud Powell sound. Do you hear swing and space?

artiest/renee-fleming.text:
Renée Fleming is an American soprano and actress, born on 14 February 1959. She sings opera, concert works and songs, appears in the theatre and in films, and performs at major public occasions. She has a full lyric soprano and has sung roles in Italian, German, French, Czech, Russian and her native English. In 2008 she became the first woman in the 125-year history of the Metropolitan Opera to headline, as a soloist, the opening gala of a season.

She made many albums, such as Visions of Love: Mozart Arias in 1996, The Schubert Album in 1997, Rusalka in 1998 and Strauss's Four Last Songs in 1996. A large part of her career she devoted to new music. Composers such as André Previn, Caroline Shaw, Kevin Puts, Henri Dutilleux, Brad Mehldau and Wayne Shorter wrote operas, concert pieces and songs for her. The conductor Georg Solti said that in his long life he had perhaps heard two sopranos of such quality.

She is unusual for an opera singer because she also became known outside the classical world. She sang and recorded with artists such as Luciano Pavarotti, Lou Reed, Wynton Marsalis, Paul Simon, Sting and Joe Jackson. She sang on the soundtracks of The Shape of Water and The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King, and she is the only classical singer to have sung the American national anthem at the Super Bowl. For her work she received five Grammys and the National Medal of Arts. She shows that an opera voice can also belong in pop and jazz.
artiest/renee-fleming.listen: Listen to her recording of Rusalka and notice the voice against the orchestra. Do you hear how full and warm the tone sounds?

artiest/renzo-rossellini.text:
Renzo Rossellini was an Italian composer, music critic and music teacher. He was born on 2 February 1908 in Rome and died on 13 May 1982 in Monte Carlo. His elder brother was the film director Roberto Rossellini. Many musicians and artists visited the family home, among them Franco Alfano, Pietro Mascagni, Giacomo Puccini and Ottorino Respighi. He studied at the Santa Cecilia conservatoire in Rome, worked as a critic for the newspaper Il Messaggero and taught, including at the conservatoire in Pesaro. In 1946 he was co-founder of the Italian musicians' union.

He began composing in the 1920s, his first published piece being the song Le cennamelle from 1927. His oeuvre includes some one hundred and thirty film scores, ten operas, four ballets, two oratorios, cantatas, symphonies, chamber music and vocal music. He wrote the music for several of his brother's films, including Rome, Open City from 1945 and Paisan from 1946. From 1972 to 1976 he was artistic director of the Opéra de Monte-Carlo.

Rossellini is best known for his film music, which stood close to the images of Italian postwar neorealism. He also stood for a broad conception of the composer's profession: opera, ballet and concert music, alongside work for film. He shows how film music in Italy was part of ordinary musical practice.
artiest/renzo-rossellini.listen: Listen to the music for Rome, Open City and notice how the music supports the images. Does it stand out, or does it stay in the background?

artiest/return-to-forever.text:
Return to Forever was an American jazz fusion band that the pianist Chick Corea founded in 1972. The only permanent member besides him was bass player Stanley Clarke. Corea had earlier played on Miles Davis's albums In a Silent Way and Bitches Brew and then worked with the avant-garde group Circle. In 1972 he wanted to reach a larger audience and chose music more accessible than the avant-garde.

The first line-up played mainly Latin-tinged music, with the Brazilian singer Flora Purim and percussionist Airto Moreira, saxophonist Joe Farrell and Clarke on acoustic and electric bass. The debut Return to Forever came out in 1972 on ECM, with Crystal Silence and La Fiesta. Light as a Feather from 1973 included Spain. After that the group turned into an instrumental jazz rock band with electric guitar and a distorted sound. Hymn of the Seventh Galaxy appeared in 1973. Among those that followed were Where Have I Known You Before, No Mystery and Romantic Warrior. In 1977 the group stopped, although it later came together live from time to time.

Return to Forever is regarded, alongside Weather Report, The Headhunters and the Mahavishnu Orchestra, as a core of 1970s jazz fusion. The group brought musicians such as Clarke, Purim, Moreira and Al Di Meola to wider attention. In the course it stands beside Herbie Hancock's Head Hunters as proof that jazz in those years became electric and louder.
artiest/return-to-forever.listen: Listen to Spain from Light as a Feather and notice the electric piano and the Latin rhythms. Do you hear how the solos rise above a solid rhythm?

artiest/rhythim-is-rhythim.text:
Rhythim Is Rhythim is one of the artist names of Derrick May, an American electronic musician from Belleville, Michigan, born in 1963. At secondary school he became friends with Juan Atkins and Kevin Saunderson. Together they are known as the Belleville Three, the three pioneers of Detroit techno. Their examples were the electronic sounds of Kraftwerk and the disco they heard on the radio, and they played that music at parties and in clubs.

May began his recording career in 1987 with Nude Photo and then followed it with Strings of Life, the track that made techno known worldwide. The title was given to it by Frankie Knuckles. His own label Transmat also released Kaos and It Is What It Is, most of the tracks between 1987 and 1989. In Detroit the three friends played at the club The Music Institute. Although May released little in the 1990s, he continued to DJ and helped other makers get a label, among them Carl Craig and Stacey Pullen.

Strings of Life sounds different from much dance music of the time, because strings and piano from a sampler carry the track, and not a heavy bass. In the course it is listed as a listening tip for the chapter on electronic music.
artiest/rhythim-is-rhythim.listen: Listen to Strings of Life and notice the opening: strings and piano from a sampler without a bass drum. When does the rhythm come in, and what changes then?

artiest/rhythim-is-rhythim-derrick-may.text:
Rhythim Is Rhythim is the best-known production alias of Derrick May, an American electronic musician from Belleville, Michigan, born in 1963. At secondary school he became friends with Juan Atkins and Kevin Saunderson. Together they are known as The Belleville Three, the pioneers of Detroit techno. Atkins taught him to DJ, they listened to the radio show of The Electrifying Mojo and drew inspiration from Kraftwerk and disco. May later called his own sound Hi-Tek Soul, a blend of George Clinton and Kraftwerk stuck in an elevator. He also named Yellow Magic Orchestra, Ryuichi Sakamoto and Ultravox as influences.

His own label was called Transmat, with Fragile as a second label for work with more samples. Under the name Rhythim Is Rhythim, tracks such as Nude Photo, Kaos, It Is What It Is and Strings of Life appeared between 1987 and 1989. The last of these became his best-known track. Frankie Knuckles, who gave the record its name, described how hard it hit in the clubs. Remarkably, the piece has no bass line: the tension comes from tight percussion and a driving sequence of piano chords, supplemented by strings from the synthesizer.

May also mentored younger makers, among them Carl Craig and Stacey Pullen. His residency at The Music Institute in Detroit became a meeting place for a mixed audience. His work often received more recognition in Britain and the rest of Europe than at home. In this way he became a key figure for later dance and rave culture. He has been called the Miles Davis of techno.
artiest/rhythim-is-rhythim-derrick-may.listen: Listen to Strings of Life and notice what is missing: a bass line. Follow how the driving piano chords and the percussion together build the tension, and how the strings join in more and more.

artiest/riad-al-sunbati.text:
Riad Mohamed El Sunbati, also spelled Riad Sonbati, was an Egyptian composer and musician, born on 30 November 1906 and died on 10 September 1981. He was regarded as one of the great names of Egyptian music and composed 539 works for the Egyptian opera, operettas and Egyptian film. He also wrote religious music and song lyrics.

He was the first son after eight daughters. His father was a singer at parties and weddings and caught him as a child playing the oud and singing Sayed Darwish. He took him along as a wedding singer. At the age of nine he developed an eye disease, but his talent was obvious. He became lead singer of a group and was given the nickname the nightingale of Mansoura. In 1928 he moved with his father to Cairo, where he was hired as a teacher of oud and singing at the Arab Music Institute. After three years he switched to composing. His first composition was a poem by Ahmed Shawqi, later sung by Mohammed Abdel Wahab. In the early 1930s he recorded taksims for the label Odeon, oud improvisations of his own.

He wrote for many male and female singers, among them Umm Kulthum, Fairouz, Asmahan, Warda Al-Jazairia and Fayza Ahmed. His music builds on the oud and the Arabic vocal tradition. Through the voice of Umm Kulthum his work reached a large audience in the Arab world.
artiest/riad-al-sunbati.listen: Listen to an oud taksim by Sunbati and notice the sound of the oud. Do you hear how a single instrument can tell a whole story?

artiest/riccardo-chailly.text:
Riccardo Chailly is an Italian conductor, born on 20 February 1953 in Milan. He comes from a musical family. His father Luciano was a composer and administrator, among other things music director of La Scala. Riccardo studied composition with his father and at the conservatoires of Milan and Perugia, but then chose conducting, under Piero Guarino and Franco Ferrara. In his youth he also played drums in a free jazz group. From 1973 he was assistant to Claudio Abbado at La Scala, where he made his debut in 1978 with Massenet's Werther.

He was chief conductor of the Radio-Symphonie-Orchester Berlin, of the Teatro Comunale in Bologna, of the Royal Concertgebouw Orchestra from 1988 to 2004 and of the Gewandhaus Orchestra from 2005 to 2016. He is now music director of the Lucerne Festival Orchestra and of La Scala. With the Concertgebouw Orchestra he played the standard works, in particular of Bruckner and Mahler, and greatly extended the small twentieth-century repertoire.

For thirty years he recorded exclusively for Decca. His recordings from the 1980s show his breadth: operas such as Il turco in Italia and Andrea Chénier, Carmina Burana in 1984, works by Prokofiev and Stravinsky, and Rossini's Guillaume Tell. He showed that a conductor who performs both old and new music can renew an orchestra.
artiest/riccardo-chailly.listen: Listen to his 1984 recording of Carmina Burana and notice the opening, where choir and orchestra begin with an enormous crash. Do you hear how the rhythms keep coming back?

artiest/riccardo-muti.text:
Riccardo Muti is an Italian conductor, born on 28 July 1941 in Naples. He spent his youth in Molfetta, near Bari. He studied piano at the San Pietro a Majella conservatoire in Naples and then composition and conducting in Milan. He also studied composition with Nino Rota, whom he regards as a mentor. In 1967 he won the Guido Cantelli conducting competition and a year later he became chief conductor of the Maggio Musicale Fiorentino, a post he held for eleven years.

From 1971 he often conducted at the Salzburg Festival, where he became known above all for his Mozart operas. In 1973 he succeeded Otto Klemperer as chief conductor of the Philharmonia Orchestra in London. From 1979 he was music director of the Philadelphia Orchestra, from 1986 of the Filarmonica della Scala in Milan, and later also of the Chicago Symphony Orchestra, where he became music director emeritus in 2023. He now leads the Orchestra Giovanile Luigi Cherubini.

He recorded a great deal, from Aida in 1974 and La traviata in 1982 to The Rite of Spring in 1979, Carmina Burana in 1980 and Mussorgsky-Ravel Pictures at an Exhibition. He is associated above all with Verdi. He received two Grammys and in 2015, according to a Bachtrack poll, ranked fifth among the best living conductors. Muti shows that opera and symphonic work reinforce each other, and that traditions keep their value when they are played with seriousness.
artiest/riccardo-muti.listen: Listen to a recording by Muti of a Verdi opera, such as La traviata, and notice how orchestra and singers breathe together. Do you hear how the tempo moves with the emotion?

artiest/richard-bonynge.text:
Richard Bonynge is an Australian conductor and pianist, born on 29 September 1930 in Epping, a suburb of Sydney. He studied piano at the Sydney Conservatorium and received a scholarship for the Royal College of Music in London. He let it lapse in order to continue studying privately and to coach singers. One of them was Joan Sutherland, whom he had accompanied in Australia. They married in 1954 and gave opera recitals together.

In 1962 Bonynge stepped in as conductor of a recital because the scheduled conductor was ill and the replacement was in a car accident. From that moment he conducted virtually all of his wife's performances, until her farewell in 1990. His debut as an opera conductor was in 1963 in Vancouver with Faust. That same year he conducted Norma there for the first time, with Sutherland and Marilyn Horne. In his research into Massenet and the Italian bel canto composers he discovered that Massenet considered his opera Esclarmonde his best work. He bought the score and persuaded Sutherland to sing the role. The opera was performed in 1974 in San Francisco and in 1976 at the Metropolitan Opera. His debut at the Met was on 12 December 1966.

He conducted the English Chamber Orchestra on many recordings, such as La sonnambula, Norma, Lucia di Lammermoor and Rigoletto, and in 1977 founded the Vancouver Opera Orchestra. Bonynge made sure that forgotten operas could be heard again.
artiest/richard-bonynge.listen: Listen to a bel canto aria on a recording from his album Arias from Forgotten Operas and notice how the conductor lets the orchestra sing along with the soprano.

artiest/richard-d-james.text:
Richard David James is a British musician, composer and DJ, born in 1971 in Limerick, Ireland, to Welsh parents. He grew up in Cornwall and began making music at fourteen. In the late 1980s he DJed at free parties in the south-west of England. Under the name Aphex Twin he grew into one of the most idiosyncratic makers in electronic music.

His first EP, Analogue Bubblebath, came out in 1991. That same year he founded the label Rephlex with a friend. The debut album Selected Ambient Works 85-92 followed in 1992. He then signed with Warp and released, among other things, Selected Ambient Works Volume II, the Richard D. James Album in 1996, and singles such as Come to Daddy and Windowlicker, with music videos by Chris Cunningham. Drukqs followed in 2001 and Syro in 2014. He also uses other names, such as AFX and Caustic Window.

His music takes in techno, ambient, acid and jungle and is often counted as intelligent dance music. One track is calm and dreamy, another fast and messy. Critics call him one of the most influential artists in electronic music. In the course he appears with the track Xtal from 1992, a listening tip for the chapter on electronic music.
artiest/richard-d-james.listen: Listen to Xtal and notice the absence of a peak or drop. The music keeps moving calmly instead of building towards a climax.

artiest/richard-dorfmeister.text:
Richard Dorfmeister is one half of Kruder & Dorfmeister, an Austrian duo that became known for downtempo and trip hop, above all with remixes of pop, hip hop and drum and bass. The other half is Peter Kruder. The duo took its name from its two members.

In 1993 their first EP appeared, G-Stoned, with the hypnotic track High Noon. The sleeve resembled that of the album Bookends by Simon & Garfunkel. The record received good reviews especially in the United Kingdom, and Gilles Peterson was the first to play the track on his BBC programme Worldwide. The duo also had a label of its own, G-Stone Recordings.

In 2007 Nokia asked the duo to make a series of ringtones and sounds for the luxury phones Nokia 8800 Arte and Sapphire Arte. In 2010 the duo and the label celebrated their sixteenth anniversary with the compilation Sixteen F**king Years Of G-Stone Recordings and the live series K&D Sessions Live. Visual artist Fritz Fitzke and the MCs Earl Zinger and MC Ras T-Weed also took part in it. With performances at, among others, The Big Chill and the Berlin Festival, the live show grew into a world tour.

The duo's work shows that a remix can be an art form in its own right: an existing track is given a new, slow and atmospheric sound, and so becomes something new.
artiest/richard-dorfmeister.listen: Listen to High Noon by Kruder & Dorfmeister and notice the slow tempo and the repeating, hypnotic layers. What do you hear coming back again and again?

artiest/richard-egarr.text:
Richard Egarr is a British conductor and keyboard player, born on 7 August 1963 in Lincoln. He received his first training as a chorister at York Minster and at Chetham's School of Music, was an organ scholar at Clare College, Cambridge, and then studied at the Guildhall School of Music and Drama. Working with Gustav Leonhardt brought him even closer to historically informed performance.

Egarr is best known as a specialist in Baroque music, but plays much more besides. His repertoire runs from fifteenth-century organ arrangements and Dussek and Chopin on period pianos to Berg and Maxwell Davies on the modern piano. He recorded solo albums of keyboard music for, among others, Harmonia Mundi and chamber music for Hyperion. His albums from the 1990s include Complete Keyboard Works and Concertos pour clavecin et cordes.

In 2006 he became music director of the Academy of Ancient Music, a post he held until 2021. In 2007 he made his debut at Glyndebourne with a staged Matthäus-Passion by Bach. From 2020 until 2024 he was music director of the Philharmonia Baroque Orchestra in San Francisco. Since 2019 he has been principal guest conductor of the Residentie Orkest in The Hague. He lives in Amsterdam and led the Academy of the Begijnhof there. Egarr shows that a harpsichordist can also lead an orchestra, and that early music can sound like music of today.
artiest/richard-egarr.listen: Listen to a harpsichord recording by Egarr and notice the sound of the plucked strings. Do you hear that the instrument does not let the tone swell slowly the way a piano does?

artiest/richard-maltby-jr.text:
Richard Maltby Jr. is an American theatre director, producer, lyricist and screenwriter, born on 6 October 1937 in Ripon, Wisconsin. His father Richard Maltby Sr. was a well-known bandleader. At Yale he began working with the composer David Shire. Their first Broadway credit was in 1968, when their song The Girl of the Minute was used in the revue New Faces of 1968.

He conceived and directed the only two musical revues that won the Tony Award for best musical: Ain't Misbehavin' in 1978 and Fosse in 1999. With Shire he wrote, among other things, Baby in 1983, Closer Than Ever in 1989 and Big in 1996. In 1977 the Manhattan Theatre Club turned their earlier songs into the revue Starting Here, Starting Now. For Miss Saigon he wrote the lyrics together with others, which earned him a Tony nomination for best score in 1991. He also directed Song and Dance with Bernadette Peters in 1986, conceived Ring of Fire, a musical about Johnny Cash, in 2006 and co-wrote The Pirate Queen. In 2025 About Time premiered, the sequel to his earlier revues with Shire.

In addition, since 1976 he has set the monthly cryptic crossword for Harper's Magazine. Maltby is an example of a lyricist who shapes musical theatre, not only with his songs but also as a director.
artiest/richard-maltby-jr.listen: Listen to a song from Miss Saigon and notice how the lyrics move the story forward. Can you follow the character's feelings without knowing the rest of the musical?

artiest/richard-nunns.text:
Richard Nunns was a Māori instrumentalist of Pākehā descent, born on 7 December 1945 in Napier and died on 7 June 2021. He was best known for his playing of taonga pūoro, the traditional instruments of the Māori. As a young teacher in the Waikato he helped build a marae, which kindled his interest in Māori culture. He was a jazz musician at the time.

For years he played together with Hirini Melbourne, who lived from 1949 to 2003. Together they researched these instruments, which had not been played for more than a century, because their use had disappeared from the tradition in the twentieth century. Many instruments still lay in museums, and nobody knew any more how they were played. The two are regarded as those who breathed new life into this piece of Māori culture. After Melbourne's death Nunns was regarded as the greatest authority in the field. In 1998 he co-led the musicians at a ceremony at sunrise on the opening day of Te Papa.

He recorded with musicians from many styles, among them Moana and the Moahunters, the New Zealand Symphony Orchestra, King Kapisi and Salmonella Dub, and toured with, among others, Evan Parker and Marilyn Crispell. He also contributed to the music of the The Lord of the Rings films and Whale Rider. His albums include Te Kū Te Whē from 1994, Rangirua from 2001 and Utterance from 2017. In 2009 he received the Arts Laureate Award.
artiest/richard-nunns.listen: Listen to a recording of Richard Nunns on taonga pūoro, for example from Te Kū Te Whē. Notice the sounds that resemble flutes, wind and voices: which instruments do you hear?

artiest/richard-nunns-en-hirini-melbourn.text:
Richard Nunns and Hirini Melbourne were two New Zealand musicians who together brought back a nearly vanished tradition: the music of the taonga pūoro, the traditional Māori instruments. Nunns was born in 1945 in Napier, a Pākehā of Scandinavian descent in a musical family. In his younger years he was a jazz musician and worked as a teacher. When he helped build a marae in the Waikato, his interest in Māori culture grew. Melbourne, born in 1949, was himself Māori and died in 2003.

Both researched instruments that had not been played for well over a century, because their use had disappeared in the course of the twentieth century. Many instruments still lay in museums, but nobody knew any more how to play them. The pair are regarded as the founders of the revival of this part of Māori culture. After Melbourne's death Nunns was regarded as the foremost expert on these instruments in the world. He collected more than seventy of them, flutes and percussion instruments, and died in 2021.

The sound of this music is soft, breathy and close to nature. Flutes, voices and other wind and percussion instruments sound without the familiar scales of Western music. Nunns later worked with very diverse musicians, from the New Zealand Symphony Orchestra and jazz players to Salmonella Dub, and contributed to the soundtracks of The Lord of the Rings and Whale Rider. In 2009 Nunns and Melbourne were inducted together into the New Zealand Music Hall of Fame.
artiest/richard-nunns-en-hirini-melbourn.listen: Listen to Hau and notice the instruments: they are not ordinary flutes or drums, but traditional Māori instruments. Notice how breathy and soft the sound is and how much silence remains between the sounds.

artiest/richard-o-brien.text:
Richard O'Brien, born Richard Timothy Smith on 25 March 1942, is a British-New Zealand actor, writer and singer. He was born in Cheltenham and emigrated at the age of ten with his family to Tauranga in New Zealand, where his father had bought a sheep farm. He worked as a hairdresser for the Embassy Theatre in Hamilton, where he saw many late shows and got the idea for The Rocky Horror Picture Show. In 1964 he returned to England, where, thanks to his horse riding, he got a start as a stuntman in Carry On Cowboy. He took his mother's surname.

In 1970 he spent nine months in the touring production of Hair. In 1973 he wrote the musical The Rocky Horror Show, which has been performed continuously ever since. For the 1975 film adaptation, The Rocky Horror Picture Show, he co-wrote the screenplay with director Jim Sharman and himself played Riff Raff. He also co-wrote the musical film Shock Treatment from 1981. He also acted in Flash Gordon, Spice World, Dark City and Ever After.

From 1990 to 1993 he presented the Channel 4 game show The Crystal Maze, and he voiced Lawrence Fletcher in the series Phineas and Ferb. In 2011 he also received New Zealand citizenship. The music of Rocky Horror, full of rock 'n' roll and science fiction, became a cult classic.
artiest/richard-o-brien.listen: Listen to a song from The Rocky Horror Picture Show, such as Time Warp, and notice how the lyrics give the dance instructions. Do you hear the influence of 1950s rock 'n' roll?

artiest/richard-robbins.text:
Richard Robbins was an American composer who became known as the regular film composer of Merchant Ivory Productions. He was born in 1940 in Weymouth, Massachusetts, and began playing the piano at the age of five. He studied at the New England Conservatory in Boston and then received a scholarship to continue his studies in Vienna. Later he headed the Mannes School of Music in New York. He drew inspiration from the compositions of Philip Glass.

In 1976 he met Ismail Merchant, the co-founder of Merchant Ivory. Robbins wrote and directed for him the short documentary Sweet Sounds about the Mannes School. In 1979 he composed the music for The Europeans. From that moment he became the company's musical director and wrote the music for almost all of their films, including Heat and Dust, The Bostonians, A Room with a View, Maurice, Howards End and The Remains of the Day. For the last two he received Oscar nominations, in 1992 and 1993. For Maurice he won the Golden Osella.

His film music suits the costume dramas he worked on: restrained, elegant and often built around piano and strings. He gave those films a clear, refined sound, without the music drowning out the images. Robbins died in 2012 in Rhinebeck, New York, of Parkinson's disease. His work shows how a composer and a director duo could build a single style over many years, so that the music became almost a signature of the company.
artiest/richard-robbins.listen: Listen to The Pensione Bertollini and notice how the music evokes the atmosphere of the film. Look for the instruments that carry the melody and ask yourself whether the music sounds cheerful or wistful.

artiest/richard-rodgers.text:
Richard Rodgers was an American composer who wrote mainly for the musical theatre. He was born on 28 June 1902 in Queens, New York, and died on 30 December 1979. He began playing the piano at the age of six and from 1921 studied composition at the Institute of Musical Art, later the Juilliard School. He wrote 43 Broadway musicals and more than nine hundred songs and was one of the best-known American composers of the twentieth century.

He first worked with the lyricist Lorenz Hart, in the 1920s and 1930s, on, among others, A Connecticut Yankee, On Your Toes, Babes in Arms and Pal Joey. Then, with Oscar Hammerstein II in the 1940s and 1950s, he wrote Oklahoma!, Carousel, South Pacific, The King and I, Cinderella, Flower Drum Song and The Sound of Music. It is above all the collaboration with Hammerstein that is praised for bringing the Broadway musical to maturity, with stories that revolve around characters and drama rather than light entertainment. Rodgers also wrote the music for the television series Victory at Sea.

He was the first to win an Emmy, a Grammy, an Oscar and a Tony, the later EGOT, and a Pulitzer Prize as well. In 1978 he was among the first group of winners of the Kennedy Center Honors. His songs were played not only in the theatre but also by pop singers and jazz musicians, and so influenced popular music.
artiest/richard-rodgers.listen: Listen to a song from Oklahoma! or The Sound of Music and notice how the melody reflects the character's mood. Which words and which notes belong together?

artiest/richard-stannard.text:
Richard Stannard, nicknamed Biff, is a British songwriter and producer, born in 1966. He works with Julian Gallagher and Ash Howes in the Brighton-based production team Biffco. His breakthrough came with the boy band East 17. Stannard got to know the singer and writer Tony Mortimer and put him in touch with the manager Tom Watkins. He was executive producer of the debut album Walthamstow from 1992 and produced two tracks of the follow-up Steam from 1994.

After that he wrote and produced for a long list of pop acts. The team worked for, among others, Kylie Minogue, One Direction, Atomic Kitten, Ellie Goulding, Leona Lewis, Little Mix, Sophie Ellis-Bextor and Will Young. The rise of the Spice Girls, Five and East 17 in particular is largely credited to them. Since 2010 Stannard and Howes also worked as musical director and producer of the songs on the British TV programme The X Factor. In 2010 Stannard founded, with two business partners, the label Major Label, which was the first to sign the synth-pop duo Hurts.

In the course Stannard appears as one of the writers of Wannabe, the first single by the Spice Girls from the summer of 1996, which the five singers wrote together with Matt Rowe and him. He is an example of the pop makers who work behind the scenes and shape other people's hits.
artiest/richard-stannard.listen: Listen to Wannabe and notice the rhythm of the verses, in which the singers take turns speaking and singing quickly. How does the chorus then make the song easy to sing along to?

artiest/richard-strauss.text: Richard Strauss, from Munich, made his name with symphonic poems in the wake of Liszt and Wagner and then wrote mainly operas. He was a virtuoso of the orchestra and could depict almost anything with instruments, from a flock of sheep to a hero. Also sprach Zarathustra from 1896, after Nietzsche, opens with a sunrise that was made world-famous by the film 2001: A Space Odyssey. With Salome and Elektra he stretched tonality to the limit.
artiest/richard-strauss.listen: Listen to the sunrise and hear how three trumpet notes rise from a deep, low tone, followed by the whole orchestra and the timpani.

artiest/richard-wagner.text: Richard Wagner wanted to merge music, poetry and drama into a single total work of art and wrote the texts of his music dramas himself. He worked with leitmotifs, short themes that return with characters and ideas, and let the music flow on without separate numbers. The chord at the beginning of Tristan und Isolde, completed in 1859, does not resolve and unsettled harmony. In Bayreuth he had a theatre of his own built, where in 1876 the complete Ring des Nibelungen was heard.
artiest/richard-wagner.listen: Listen to the first bars of Tristan und Isolde and hear how the yearning chord lingers after the cellos without resolving.

artiest/richie-havens.text:
Richie Havens was an American singer, songwriter and guitarist, born on 21 January 1941 in Bedford-Stuyvesant in Brooklyn and died on 22 April 2013. He was the eldest of nine children. His father had Blackfoot ancestors, his mother came from the British West Indies. As a boy he formed a doo-wop group with friends on the street corner, and at sixteen he sang with the McCrea Gospel Singers. At twenty he left for Greenwich Village, where he first recited poems, drew portraits and heard folk in the clubs, before he picked up a guitar.

His solo performances quickly spread beyond the Village. He signed with Albert Grossman, Bob Dylan's manager, and got a contract with Verve Folkways, later Verve Forecast. There Mixed Bag appeared at the end of 1966, including a cover of Dylan's Just Like a Woman. His first single, No Opportunity Necessary, was later covered by Yes. Something Else Again from 1968 was his first album on the Billboard chart. In the years that followed came, among others, Electric Havens, Stonehenge and Alarm Clock.

His music contains folk, soul and rhythm and blues, and he played rhythm guitar, often in open tunings. He opened the Woodstock festival and sang many jingles for television commercials. He played many songs by others and gave them a rhythm of their own, which made him a recognisable figure of the 1960s folk scene.
artiest/richie-havens.listen: Listen to his cover of Just Like a Woman on Mixed Bag and notice his rhythmic guitar playing. Do you hear how the chords and the voice together make a beat of their own?

artiest/richie-powell.text:
Richie Powell was an American jazz pianist, composer and arranger, born on 5 September 1931 in New York and died on 26 June 1956. He was the youngest of three sons and the brother of the better-known pianist Bud Powell. Their father was a stride pianist, another brother a trumpeter and violinist. Bud did not help his younger brother in his development. According to one story, Richie came to the piano after he kept asking the drummer Max Roach, who lived nearby, for drum lessons, until Roach suggested he play piano. A forgotten pianist, Bob Bunyan, taught him chords, and he studied with Mary Lou Williams.

After working in Philadelphia and New York he played in the bands of Paul Williams from 1951 to 1952 and Johnny Hodges from 1952 to 1954. In the spring of 1954 he became pianist and arranger of the quintet of trumpeter Clifford Brown and drummer Max Roach. That group toured the United States for two years and made studio and live recordings, including Clifford Brown & Max Roach, which is in the Grammy Hall of Fame.

Powell was killed on 26 June 1956 in a car accident, together with his wife and Clifford Brown, during a night drive from Philadelphia to Chicago. He was just beginning to receive recognition and never recorded an album as a leader. His piano playing was playful, full of musical quotations, with a relatively heavy touch and left-hand fourths, with which he influenced the pianist McCoy Tyner.
artiest/richie-powell.listen: Listen to the album Clifford Brown & Max Roach and notice the piano beneath the trumpet solos. Do you hear a quotation from another song, or the heavy touch in the left hand?

artiest/richie-sambora.text:
Richie Sambora is an American guitarist, songwriter and singer, born on 11 July 1959 in Perth Amboy, New Jersey. He grew up in Woodbridge Township. His first instrument, at the age of six, was the accordion. At twelve he picked up the guitar, after the death of Jimi Hendrix in 1970. From an early age he was influenced by blues and the rock 'n' roll of the 1960s.

He played in the group Message, which made the independent album Lessons in 1982, later in Mercy and in Duke Williams & the Extremes. At nineteen he had an independent label of his own, Dream Disc Records. His first professional tour was as the opening act for Joe Cocker. Shortly before he joined Bon Jovi in 1983, he auditioned unsuccessfully for Kiss. At Bon Jovi he took the place of guitarist Dave Sabo, who started Skid Row. He was a member of that band from 1983 to 2013 and co-wrote many songs. In 2018 he was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame as a member of Bon Jovi.

Solo he released three albums: Stranger in This Town in 1991, Undiscovered Soul in 1998 and Aftermath of the Lowdown in 2012. In 2018 he formed the duo RSO with Orianthi, which released the album Radio Free America that year. His guitar playing belongs to the sound of 1980s stadium rock, with solid riffs and melodic solos.
artiest/richie-sambora.listen: Listen to a Bon Jovi track from the 1980s and notice the guitar solo. Do you hear how the solo picks up the melody of the chorus again?
